answer: A ridge guild assigns each agent one yarrow patch on a high trail and one cairn to keep. Each week the agent climbs to the patch, tends it, then stands at the cairn and recites a sonnet naming the patch, the trail, and the weather, while two witnesses listen and check the patch against the words. A witness strikes any name whose patch is bare or whose trail was never walked. A thousand fake names need a thousand weekly climbs, a thousand tended patches, and a thousand sonnets spoken before witnesses, and no copied verse survives a walk up the ridge.
